ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, line $AD\parallel BE\parallel CF$, if $\frac{AB}{BC}=\frac{1}{3}$, $AD=2$, and $CF=6$, then what is the length of the line segment $BE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, draw DG $\parallel$ AC through point D, intersecting CF at point G, and BE at point H, \\
$\because$ $AD\parallel BE\parallel CF$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{DE}{EF}=\frac{AB}{BC}=\frac{1}{3}$, quadrilaterals ABHD and ACGD are parallelograms, \\
$\therefore$ BH=AD=CG=2, $\frac{DE}{DF}=\frac{1}{4}$, \\
$\because$ $CF=6$, \\
$\therefore$ FG=4, \\
$\because$ BE$\parallel$CF, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle DEH\sim \triangle DFG$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{HE}{FG}=\frac{DE}{DF}=\frac{1}{4}$, \\
$\therefore$ HE=1, \\
$\therefore$ BE=BH+HE=$\boxed{3}$.

From the image, AD, BE, and CF are parallel slices between the same two sides; from the text, AD = 2, CF = 6 and AB:BC = 1:3. Because AD ∥ CF, triangles OAD and OCF are similar, so OA/OC = AD/CF = 1/3. Let AB = x and BC = 3x, so OC = OA + 4x. Solve OA/(OA+4x)=1/3, giving OA = 2x. Then OB = OA + AB = 3x and OC = 6x. ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, line $AD\parallel BE\parallel CF$, if $\frac{AB}{BC}=\frac{1}{3}$, $AD=2$, and $CF=6$, then what is the length of the line segment $BE$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, draw DG $\parallel$ AC through point D, intersecting CF at point G, and BE at point H, \\
$\because$ $AD\parallel BE\parallel CF$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{DE}{EF}=\frac{AB}{BC}=\frac{1}{3}$, quadrilaterals ABHD and ACGD are parallelograms, \\
$\therefore$ BH=AD=CG=2, $\frac{DE}{DF}=\frac{1}{4}$, \\
$\because$ $CF=6$, \\
$\therefore$ FG=4, \\
$\because$ BE$\parallel$CF, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle DEH\sim \triangle DFG$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{HE}{FG}=\frac{DE}{DF}=\frac{1}{4}$, \\
$\therefore$ HE=1, \\
$\therefore$ BE=BH+HE=$\boxed{3}$

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure there are three horizontal lines parallel to each other; the two ends of the upper horizontal line are labeled A and D, the intersections of the middle horizontal line with the two oblique lines are labeled B and E, and the intersections of the lower horizontal line are labeled C and F. A, B, C are on the same oblique straight line on the left side, and D, E, F are on the same oblique straight line on the right side; therefore AD, BE, CF are three parallel transversals caught between the same two oblique straight lines.

Reasoning: It is known that AD ∥ BE ∥ CF, AB/BC = 1/3, AD = 2, CF = 6. Because the positions cut off by parallel lines on the same transversal correspond proportionally, AB:BC = 1:3, so B is located at 1/(1+3) = 1/4 from the upper parallel line to the lower parallel line. The length of the transversal between the two straight lines along the parallel direction changes linearly with this position: the upper length is AD = 2, and the lower length is CF = 6. Therefore the middle transversal BE = AD + (1/4)(CF - AD) = 2 + (1/4)(6 - 2) = 2 + 1 = 3.
